_meta.source: KFF May 2026 implementation survey (43 states + DC responded) + state eligibility-system vendor public filings + CMS T-MSIS Technical Assessment summary 2025-Q4
_meta.purpose: Per-state composite 'ex parte verification capability' score (0-100). Higher scores indicate the state's eligibility system can verify employment, exemption status, and qualifying activity against existing administrative data without forcing the enrollee to re-prove what the state already knows. Lower scores indicate Arkansas-grade reliance on enrollee self-reporting through a portal.
_meta.scoring_formula: Observed-rate-led composite. Score A (OBSERVED ex parte, 0-100): the state's actual share of Medicaid renewals completed ex parte, from CMS eligibility-processing data (2023-03 to 2026-02), × 100. This is the dominant factor — a realized measure of auto-renewal capability, not a proxy. Score B (data sources, 0-100): wage 30pts (ui_wage 30; income-verification tools — credit-agency, consent-based — are not scored, see §3.5) + frailty 30pts (medicaid_claims 20 + behavioral_health_mco 10) + other 20pts (snap_tanf 5 + vital_records 4 + workforce_dev 4 + corrections 4 + child_welfare 3) — the work-requirement-specific feeds that income-renewal ex parte didn't test. Score C (historical churn, 0-100): round((1 - prior_section_1115_denial_rate) × 100); neutral 50 prior for states without documented prior work-requirement experience. Composite = round(0.50 × Score A + 0.35 × Score B + 0.15 × Score C). A legacy vendor-tier capability score is retained as context only and does not feed the composite. Bands: composite ≥ 70 'low churn', 45-69 'mid', < 45 'high churn'. See METHODOLOGY.md §3.5.

data_source_flags.medicaid_claims_match: State will use Medicaid claims data to auto-identify medically-frail enrollees (KFF May 2026 survey Q14).
data_source_flags.behavioral_health_mco_match: State will use behavioral health MCO enrollment to auto-identify SUD/disabling-mental-disorder exemptions (KFF Q15).
data_source_flags.ui_wage_match: State will use unemployment-insurance wage records for employment verification (T-MSIS technical assessment + KFF Q16).
data_source_flags.snap_tanf_compliance_match: State will use SNAP/TANF work-compliance rolls to auto-apply §1902(xx)(2)(F) exemption (KFF Q17).
data_source_flags.corrections_records_match: State has data-sharing agreement with state DOC for recent-incarceration exemption auto-application (KFF Q18; secondary research where unanswered).
data_source_flags.child_welfare_records_match: State will use child-welfare / vital-records data to auto-apply caregiver-of-minor exemption (KFF Q19).
data_source_flags.self_attestation_accepted: State will accept enrollee self-attestation (with subsequent audit) for activity hours and exemption status, as federally permitted under §1902(xx)(4)(D) (KFF Q20). v4 note: this flag now contributes to Score A (core capability — self_attestation_policy 0-15) rather than Score B (data sources), reflecting that self-attestation is a state policy lever, not a data source.
data_source_flags.vital_records_match: State vital-records department integration with the eligibility system. Drives pregnancy exemption auto-application via birth-registry feeds and supports caregiver-of-minor verification independently of child-welfare records. v4 addition; research-in-progress, only documented top-tier states populated TRUE.
data_source_flags.workforce_dev_records_match: State DOL / WIOA training database integration. Drives qualifying-activity auto-verification for adults in approved workforce-development programs (OBBBA §1902(xx)(2)(C)). v4 addition; research-in-progress, only documented top-tier states populated TRUE.

_meta.integration_bonus_basis: States with documented modern integrated eligibility systems (CalSAWS, IES, IE, HBE) and prior CMS Innovator-pathway grants for data integration get a 20-point bonus reflecting that the 'will use' flags are operationally backed. States with legacy systems (MMIS-only, late-generation Cúram, in-house) where T-MSIS quality scores in 2024 were below the median get 0 bonus.
_meta.non_expansion_states: 10 non-expansion states (AL, FL, GA, KS, MS, SC, TN, TX, WI, WY) receive score=null. The OBBBA work requirement does not apply to their working-age Medicaid population through the expansion pathway.
_meta.uncertainty: The observed ex parte rate measures realized income/eligibility auto-renewal during the unwinding — necessary but not sufficient for work-requirement verification, which also needs the hours and exemption feeds captured in Score B. Treat the composite as a relative state-by-state ranking, not a prediction of work-requirement admin-churn rates. Score C is documented for the four states with prior Section 1115 work-requirement experience (AR, NH, GA, KY) and is a neutral 50 prior elsewhere.
_meta.observed_ex_parte_source: CMS State Medicaid & CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov 5abea2e0), share of completed renewals conducted ex parte, volume-weighted 2023-03 to 2026-02. National ~66.6%.

historical_experience.people_affected: ~18,164 dropped of ~60,700 subject (ages 30-49, Dec 2018) in 9 months
historical_experience.primary_source: Sommers, BD, et al. 2019. "Medicaid Work Requirements — Results from the First Year in Arkansas." NEJM 381:1073-1082. doi:10.1056/NEJMsr1901772
historical_experience.context_note: Arkansas's 2018 Section 1115 demonstration was the only state where work-requirement disenrollments actually happened at scale before federal courts halted further implementation. ~18,164 of the ~60,700 adults subject in a given month (ages 30-49, Dec 2018) lost coverage — roughly 30% of those subject, about 18% of the ~100,000 targeted (Sommers et al. 2019, NEJM). That ~30% per-cycle procedural-denial rate is a reasonable ceiling-of-what-can-go-wrong reference for OBBBA, given that Arkansas was an early implementer with limited time and integration.

historical_experience.context_note: New Hampshire's Granite Advantage work requirement reached one month of active enforcement before federal court halt. ~17K of 25K subject enrollees were reportedly heading for non-compliance disenrollment when stopped.
